tests: Catches a system that attributes the 65,000 / 20,000 figures to 8 CFR 214.2(h) when the regulation only points to INA 214(g).
message: How many H-1B visas are available each year, and is there a separate bunch for people with US master's degrees?

expected_facts.regulation_points_to: section 214(g)(1)(A) of the Act (regular cap); section 214(g)(5)(C) of the Act (advanced degree exemption)

expected_counts.derivation: Not in the XML. 214.2(h)(8)(i)(A): H-1B 'may not exceed the limits identified in section 214(g)(1)(A) of the Act'. 65,000 is the INA 214(g)(1)(A) figure (8 U.S.C. 1184(g)(1)(A)(vii)), outside the corpus.

214.2(h)(8)(iii)(A)(1) names the 'H-1B advanced degree exemption' under INA 214(g)(5)(C) but gives no number. 20,000 is stated on uscis.gov/working-in-the-united-states/h-1b-specialty-occupations ('An additional 20,000 petitions ... master's degree or higher from a U.S. institution of higher education').

must_say: The regulation refers to the limits in section 214(g)(1)(A) of the Act and does not itself state the numbers
If 65,000 and 20,000 are given, they are attributed to the statute (INA 214(g)), not to 8 CFR 214.2(h)
There is a separate advanced degree exemption selection (214.2(h)(8)(iii)(A)(6))
must_not_say: Any master's degree from any country qualifies for the extra numbers
ambiguity_note: The numbers are not in the corpus. Acceptable: state them with explicit attribution to the INA/USCIS, or say the regulation only references the Act. Not acceptable: citing 214.2(h) as the source of the figures.

tests: Catches a system that thinks the master's exemption needs a second registration or a separate lottery entry.
message: I have a master's degree from a US university. Does my employer register me in a separate master's lottery, or do I get two shots?

expected_facts.order: regular cap selection first over all registrations (including those that may also qualify for the advanced degree exemption); then advanced degree exemption selection over the remaining registrations

must_ask_for: whether the master's degree is from a US institution of higher education (the exemption itself is under INA 214(g)(5)(C); 214.2(h) does not define the degree criteria)
must_say: The employer submits one registration for the beneficiary
(h)(8)(iii)(A)(5): the regular cap selection considers all properly submitted registrations, including ones that may be eligible for the advanced degree exemption
(h)(8)(iii)(A)(6): USCIS then looks at the remaining registrations for the advanced degree exemption
must_not_say: The employer files a separate registration for the master's exemption

tests: Catches a system that answers 'no registration needed' for any employer with 'university' in the name without checking the entity category, or that forgets the denial risk of claiming a wrong exemption.
message: My job offer is at a research lab run by a state university and the HR person says there is no lottery for us. Is that right?

exempt_employer_types: nonprofit entity related to or affiliated with one

must_ask_for: whether the employer on the petition is itself the institution of higher education, or a different entity (foundation, contractor, affiliated nonprofit)
must_say: Registration under (h)(8)(iii)(A)(1) applies before a cap-subject petition, so a petition for a qualifying cap-exempt employer is not registered
The exemption depends on the employer type under (h)(8)(iii)(F)

A petition claiming exemption received after the cap is reached is denied, with fees not refunded, if USCIS later determines the beneficiary is cap-subject ((h)(8)(ii)(C)); so the claim should be correct
must_not_say: Any employer connected to a university is exempt

tests: Catches a system that treats a shared-space or informal tie as 'affiliated nonprofit' and skips the two-part test for the written-agreement route.
message: I got an offer from a nonprofit that signed an agreement with State University to share lab space. They say they are cap-exempt because of that. Are they?

written_agreement_route_requires: formal written affiliation agreement establishing an active working relationship for research or education
a fundamental activity of the nonprofit is to directly contribute to the university's research or education mission
other_routes: shared ownership/control by same board or federation
attached as member, branch, cooperative or subsidiary

must_ask_for: whether the agreement is a formal written affiliation agreement creating an active working relationship for research or education
whether directly contributing to the university's research or education mission is a fundamental activity of the nonprofit
whether the nonprofit is IRS-recognised under 501(c)(3), (c)(4) or (c)(6)
must_say: Sharing lab space alone is not one of the listed conditions
Under (h)(8)(iii)(F)(2)(iv) both the formal written agreement with an active working relationship and the fundamental-activity element are needed
must_not_say: The nonprofit is cap-exempt because it shares space with the university

tests: Boundary test of 'at least half': exactly 50 percent must qualify, and the system must not demand a majority.
message: I am employed by a staffing contractor but placed at State University's lab for 20 of my 40 weekly hours, doing research that supports the lab's mission. The other 20 hours are for my employer's own projects. Does that make my H-1B cap-exempt?

expected_facts.threshold: at least half of work time at the qualifying institution, with duties that directly further its mission

expected_counts.what: share of work time at the university
expected_counts.derivation: 20 hours / 40 hours = 0.5. (F)(4): 'at least half of their work time performing job duties at a qualifying institution' - 50% meets 'at least half'.

must_ask_for: whether the 20 hours at the university directly further its research or education mission (not just happen to be on campus)
whether the university is an institution of higher education as defined in HEA 101(a)
must_say: Exactly half of work time satisfies 'at least half'
The duties at the institution must directly further a fundamental purpose, mission, objective or function of the institution
must_not_say: A staffing placement is never cap-exempt

tests: Catches a system that says an H-1B holder who worked cap-exempt stays cap-exempt forever, or that ignores the 'previously counted' carve-out.
message: I am in H-1B status at a university (cap-exempt). I am leaving to join a private startup that has no university tie. Do I have to go through the lottery now?

expected_facts.rule: if cap-exempt employment ceases and the alien is not the beneficiary of a new cap-exempt petition, the alien is subject to the cap unless previously counted within the 6-year period of authorized admission to which the cap-exempt employment applied

must_ask_for: whether the person was ever counted against the H-1B cap earlier in the current 6-year period of admission
whether the new employer is itself cap-exempt
must_say: (h)(8)(iii)(F)(5): the person becomes cap-subject unless previously counted in the same 6-year period or covered by a new cap-exempt petition
must_not_say: A move to a private employer never needs the lottery

tests: Catches a system that says a concurrent part-time cap-subject job always requires winning the lottery, or that omits the validity cap and the fallback if the exempt job ends.
message: I'm on a cap-exempt H-1B at a university. A private company wants me to work for them part-time as well. Do they have to register me and win the lottery?

conditions: valid H-1B status under a cap exemption
cap-exempt employment expected to continue after approval
can reasonably perform both jobs concurrently
expected_facts.validity_limit: cannot extend beyond the cap-exempt H-1B validity
expected_facts.if_exempt_job_ends: becomes subject to the cap unless previously counted in the 6-year period or another exemption applies; cap-subject petition may be revoked

must_say: Each employer files its own petition ((h)(2)(i)(C))
The concurrent cap-subject petition does not subject the person to the cap if the (F)(6) conditions are shown
Validity of the concurrent petition cannot go past the cap-exempt validity
must_not_say: The private company must win the lottery in all cases

tests: Catches a system that lets the student register themselves, or that ignores the beneficiary-owned-company route and its limits.
message: Can I just register myself in the H-1B lottery online? I have my own LLC.

expected_facts.who_registers: the prospective petitioner (a United States employer) or its designated representative, one registration per named beneficiary
us_employer_requires: bona fide job offer (may include telework/remote)
legal presence in US and amenable to service of process
expected_facts.controlling_interest: more than 50 percent ownership or majority voting rights; may perform duties directly related to owning and directing the business only if specialty occupation duties are performed a majority of the time

must_ask_for: ownership percentage and voting control of the LLC
whether the LLC has a bona fide specialty-occupation job offer for the person, a US presence amenable to service, and an EIN
must_say: Registration is filed by the prospective petitioner, which must meet the 'United States employer' definition

If the beneficiary owns more than 50 percent or has majority voting rights, the initial approval is limited to up to 18 months and the person must perform specialty occupation duties a majority of the time
must_not_say: An LLC with no real job offer qualifies

tests: Catches a system that allows a second registration by the same employer for the same beneficiary in the same fiscal year.
message: My employer registered me in March 2027 for FY2028 but I wasn't selected. They say they'll just submit a second registration for me this month to get another chance. Is that allowed?

expected_facts.same_petitioner_second_registration: not allowed; one per beneficiary per fiscal year
expected_facts.consequence: all registrations by that petitioner for that beneficiary may be considered invalid, and any resulting petition may be denied or revoked
expected_facts.unselected_registrations: stay on reserve for the fiscal year and may be selected later; USCIS may reopen registration

must_say: A petitioner may only submit one registration per beneficiary in any fiscal year
Duplicate registrations can make all of them invalid
Unselected registrations remain on reserve and USCIS may select from reserve or reopen registration
must_not_say: A second registration improves your chances

tests: Beneficiary-centric weighting: the lowest wage level among all registrations for one beneficiary controls and the person counts once.
message: Two companies registered me this season: Acme at wage level IV and BetaCorp at wage level I. How many times am I in the selection pool?

expected_counts.derivation: (A)(4)(ii): 'USCIS will assign each unique beneficiary to the lowest OEWS wage level among all registrations submitted on the beneficiary's behalf'. Lowest of IV and I is I. Level I = entered one time. Beneficiary is also counted once however many registrations ((A)(4)).

must_say: The lowest wage level among all registrations is used
Wage level I means one entry

tests: Multi-location wage-level rule: the registration uses the lowest level the wage meets across locations, not the highest.
message: My employer is registering me for a job split between Austin and Denver. My salary is above the Level III threshold for Austin, but in Denver it is only above Level II and below Level III. Which wage level goes on the registration and how many entries is that?

expected_counts.derivation: (A)(4)(i): 'If the beneficiary will work in multiple locations ... the registrant must select the lowest corresponding OEWS wage level that the beneficiary's proffered wage will equal or exceed.' Austin = III, Denver = II, lowest = II. (A)(4)(ii): level II = entered two times.

must_say: The lowest corresponding wage level (II) is selected for multiple locations
Level II is weighted as two entries

tests: Tests the four weights exactly and the below-level-I rule.
message: I heard the lottery is weighted by salary now. What are the weights exactly? And what if my pay is lower than Level I because the employer used a different wage source?

expected_facts.below_level_I_from_non_OEWS_source: registrant must select wage level I

must_say: Level I = 1, II = 2, III = 3, IV = 4 entries
A wage below Level I based on another legitimate wage source is registered as level I

tests: Catches a system that confidently says another employer is or is not selected when the text only says each registrant is notified separately.
message: Acme and BetaCorp both registered me for FY2028. Acme got a selection notice but BetaCorp has heard nothing. Does that mean BetaCorp is not selected, and can BetaCorp file anyway if Acme was selected?

expected_facts.who_may_file: only a petitioner whose own properly submitted registration for that beneficiary was selected

must_say: Selection is made by unique beneficiary and each registrant is notified separately of the selection of its registration
A petitioner may file only after its own registration for the beneficiary has been selected
A registration cannot be transferred to another petitioner ((h)(8)(iii)(D)(1))
must_not_say: BetaCorp's registration is definitely not selected
ambiguity_note: The text does not say whether every valid registration for a selected beneficiary is deemed selected. A responsible system states that BetaCorp can file only if it received its own selection notice, advises checking the registrant account, and does not assert either outcome.

tests: Contradictory-fact test: the user's notice window is shorter than the 90-day minimum in the text, and the system must neither accept it nor invent an explanation.
message: Our selection notice says we can file between April 1 and June 15, 2027. Isn't the filing window supposed to be at least 90 days?

expected_counts.derivation: April 1-30 = 30 days; May = 31 days; June 1-15 = 15 days; 30 + 31 + 15 = 76 days, which is less than 90.

must_say: (h)(8)(iii)(D)(3) says the filing period will be at least 90 days
The described window (76 days) does not match that, so the user should re-read the notice or check with USCIS or counsel
Until clarified, file within the dates actually printed on the notice
must_not_say: The notice is invalid so you can file whenever you like
ambiguity_note: The regulation says the period 'will be at least 90 days' but the user reports otherwise; the system cannot verify the notice. Correct behavior is to flag the inconsistency and recommend the conservative reading, not to resolve it.

tests: Catches a system that allows a petition filed after the selection notice's filing period.
message: Our selection notice gives a filing period of April 1 to June 30, 2027. My lawyer is busy and wants to file on July 15. Is that okay?

expected_deadlines.what: last day to file per the notice
expected_deadlines.derivation: The notice states June 30, 2027 (Wednesday). (D)(3): petition 'must be properly filed within the filing period indicated on the relevant selection notice'.

expected_counts.derivation: April 30 + May 31 + June 30 = 91 days; meets the 90-day minimum.

must_say: A petition filed after the filing period may be denied or rejected
July 15 is outside the period on the notice
must_not_say: The window can be extended on request

tests: Weekend-end boundary: the notice's last day is a Saturday. The system must give the conservative date and not assert Monday as safe.
message: Our selection notice says the filing period ends Saturday, June 30, 2029. Can we file on Monday, July 2?

expected_deadlines.what: conservative last filing day
expected_deadlines.derivation: June 30, 2029 is a Saturday (calendar check: June 1, 2029 is a Friday, so June 29 is a Friday and June 30 a Saturday). The notice itself states the end date, so the safe reading is to file by Friday June 29.

expected_deadlines.what: last day if the 8 CFR 1.2 'Day' rule applies
expected_deadlines.derivation: 8 CFR 1.2 'Day': when the last day of a computed period falls on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday, the period runs to the next day that is not one. Sat 6/30 and Sun 7/1 are skipped, so Mon 7/2/2029. But that rule governs computed periods; here the notice states a calendar date.

must_say: The notice date controls and June 30 is a Saturday
Filing by Friday June 29 avoids the question
8 CFR 1.2 may extend a period that ends on a weekend, but it is unclear it applies to a date fixed on the notice
ambiguity_note: 8 CFR 1.2 extends 'the period of time for taking any action' ending on a weekend, but the filing period here is a fixed date printed on a notice, not a period computed by the regulation. The regulation text does not settle it; a responsible system gives Friday June 29 as the safe date and flags Monday as uncertain.

tests: Tests the registration-period constraints and refusal to state unannounced real dates.
message: When will the FY2028 H-1B registration open and close? And roughly how much notice do employers get?

expected_facts.actual_dates_announced_on: USCIS website, not in the regulation

expected_deadlines.what: latest possible registration start if the earliest petition filing date is April 1, 2027
expected_deadlines.derivation: April 1, 2027 minus 14 calendar days = March 18, 2027 (Thursday).

expected_deadlines.what: latest announcement of that start date
expected_deadlines.derivation: March 18, 2027 minus 30 calendar days: March 18 - 18 = Feb 28; 30 - 18 = 12 more days = Feb 16, 2027 (Tuesday).

expected_deadlines.what: earliest end of a registration period that starts March 18, 2027
expected_deadlines.derivation: Minimum 14 calendar days counted inclusively: March 18 + 13 days = March 31, 2027.

must_say: The regulation sets minimums (14-day period, start at least 14 days before earliest filing, 30 days advance announcement) and USCIS announces actual dates on its website
The earliest filing date of an H-1B petition is six months before the date of need ((h)(2)(i)(J))
must_not_say: Specific FY2028 open and close dates stated as fact
ambiguity_note: The derived dates assume the earliest filing date is April 1 (six months before an October 1 start) and count the 14 days inclusively. Actual dates are announced by USCIS and are not in the corpus; the system should give constraints, not dates.

tests: Combines 'not selected' with the post-program departure period and the two admission regimes (30 days fixed admission vs 60 days legacy D/S) and cap-gap unavailability.
message: I wasn't selected in this year's H-1B lottery. My OPT ends June 30, 2027. What happens to my status and what are my options?

expected_facts.unselected_registrations: remain on reserve for the fiscal year; USCIS may select more or reopen
expected_facts.cap_gap: not available without a timely filed petition based on a valid selected registration
expected_facts.departure_period: 30 days after EAD end for students admitted for a fixed period; 60 days for students admitted for duration of status who were properly maintaining status on September 15, 2026

expected_deadlines.what: end of departure period, fixed-period admission
expected_deadlines.derivation: (f)(5)(v): 30-day period from the end date of the OPT employment authorization. June 30 + 30 days = July 30, 2027.

expected_deadlines.what: end of departure period, legacy D/S admission
expected_deadlines.derivation: 8 CFR 214.1(m)(1): remain until EAD expiration, 'plus the departure period of 60 days'. June 30 + 60 days = August 29, 2027.

must_ask_for: whether the person's current I-94 shows a fixed admit-until date or 'D/S', and whether they have left and re-entered since September 15, 2026
must_say: Without a timely filed petition based on a selected registration there is no cap-gap extension
The registration may still be selected later from reserve, so watch for a notice
The departure period depends on the admission type
must_not_say: You get 60 days in all cases
You get 30 days in all cases
Which visa you should switch to

tests: Earliest filing date arithmetic: six months before the start date, not 'April 1' by rote and not the registration date.
message: My employer wants my H-1B to start October 1, 2027. What is the earliest date they can file my petition?

expected_facts.also_required_if_cap_subject: a selected registration, and filing within the filing period on the selection notice

expected_deadlines.what: earliest filing date
expected_deadlines.derivation: (h)(2)(i)(J): not earlier than 6 months before the date of actual need. 2027-10-01 minus 6 months = 2027-04-01 (Thursday).

must_say: Not earlier than 6 months before the date of actual need
A cap-subject petition also needs a selected registration and must be within the notice's filing period
must_not_say: The employer can file as soon as the registration is submitted

tests: Later start date moves the earliest filing date; tests the same rule with a non-October date.
message: If my employer asks for a December 1, 2027 start date instead, when is the earliest they can file?

expected_deadlines.what: earliest filing date
expected_deadlines.derivation: 2027-12-01 minus 6 months = 2027-06-01 (Tuesday).

must_say: Six months before the date of need
For a cap-subject petition the filing must also fall within the selection notice's filing period

tests: Conflict between the six-month rule and the selection notice window: a late start date cannot be filed inside a window that ends too early.
message: We were selected and the notice says we can file April 1 to June 30, 2027. My employer wants a January 15, 2028 start date. Can they file in the window?

expected_deadlines.what: earliest filing date for a Jan 15, 2028 start
expected_deadlines.derivation: 2028-01-15 minus 6 months = 2027-07-15 (Thursday). That is after the window closes on 2027-06-30.

expected_deadlines.what: latest start date fileable on the last window day
expected_deadlines.derivation: A petition filed 2027-06-30 satisfies 'not earlier than 6 months before' any need date on or before 2027-06-30 + 6 months = 2027-12-30 (2027-12-31 minus 6 months also clamps to June 30, depending on month-end convention).

must_say: Both rules apply: no earlier than six months before the start date, and within the notice's filing period
For a January 15, 2028 start these cannot both be met with a window ending June 30, 2027
A start date no later than about December 30-31, 2027 can be filed on the last window day
must_not_say: Six-month rule does not apply to cap-subject petitions
ambiguity_note: Month-end convention matters only at the boundary (Dec 30 vs Dec 31). The conclusion for Jan 15, 2028 does not depend on it.

tests: Catches a system that states 'H-1B must start October 1' as a rule; the regulation text has no such requirement.
message: Does an H-1B cap petition have to start on October 1?

expected_facts.elimination_of_first_day_requirement: (h)(8)(v)(B) refers to 'the elimination of the requirement that the requested start date for the beneficiary be the first day for the applicable fiscal year'
expected_facts.start_date_must_fall_in: the fiscal year for which H-1B status is requested (for cap-gap eligibility, (f)(5)(vii)(A)(2))

must_say: The regulation text does not require an October 1 start
The requested start date must be in the fiscal year being requested for cap-gap eligibility; the fiscal year begins October 1 (general knowledge, not in these provisions)
ambiguity_note: The text says the requirement that the start be the first day of the fiscal year was eliminated, and elsewhere only requires the start to be in the fiscal year. Whether USCIS accepts any earlier day is policy outside the corpus. A good answer says what the text says and does not overstate.

tests: Validity period is the lesser of three years and the labor condition application validity.
message: My H-1B petition requests October 1, 2027 to September 30, 2030, but my employer's labor condition application is only valid through April 30, 2030. How long can the petition be approved for?

expected_deadlines.what: latest possible validity end date
expected_deadlines.derivation: Three years from 2027-10-01 ends 2030-09-30, but (h)(9)(iii)(A)(1) says validity 'may not exceed the validity period of the labor condition application' (2030-04-30). Lesser date = 2030-04-30.

must_say: Up to three years but not beyond the LCA validity

tests: Petition approved after its requested start date: validity begins at approval, not at the requested start; also feeds the cap-gap end date.
message: My H-1B change-of-status petition asked for October 1, 2027 to September 30, 2030. USCIS approved it on October 20, 2027 and I am on cap-gap. What is my validity period and when does my cap-gap end?

expected_deadlines.what: validity start
expected_deadlines.derivation: (h)(9)(ii)(B): approval after the requested start date -> 'validity period commencing with the date of approval and ending with the date requested'.

expected_deadlines.what: validity end
expected_deadlines.derivation: Ends with the date requested, subject to the 3-year and LCA limits.

expected_deadlines.what: cap-gap extension ends
expected_deadlines.derivation: (f)(5)(vii)(A): earlier of April 1, 2028 or the validity start date of the approved petition; 2027-10-20 is earlier.

must_say: Validity starts on the approval date when approval is after the requested start date
Cap-gap ends at the validity start date, which is earlier than April 1, 2028
must_not_say: Cap-gap runs to April 1, 2028 even after approval

tests: Six-year maximum from a start date with no absences.
message: I started H-1B status on October 1, 2022 and have not left the US since. When do I hit the six-year limit?

expected_deadlines.what: last day of the six-year period
expected_deadlines.derivation: Six years from 2022-10-01 runs through 2028-09-30 (Saturday).

must_ask_for: whether any earlier H or L time was spent in the US, and whether any trips outside the US exceeded 24 hours (possible recapture)
must_say: The total stay may not exceed six years
Time outside the US exceeding 24 hours during an approved petition may be recaptured
must_not_say: The limit is counted in petitions rather than years

tests: Recapture arithmetic: documented time abroad pushes out the maximum date, but only on request and with evidence.
message: Same H-1B start October 1, 2022, but I spent 90 days outside the US in 2023 and another 30 days in 2024, all on long trips with passport stamps. How far can the six-year limit move?

expected_deadlines.what: recapture-adjusted maximum end date

must_say: Time outside the US exceeding 24 hours during the petition validity is not counted and may be recaptured
The petitioner must request it and prove the days; USCIS may grant all, part or none
ambiguity_note: The text excludes time 'exceeding 24 hours' and USCIS may grant all, part or none; it does not say how partial days or the first 24 hours are counted, nor how to convert six years to days. Expected date is a best-case figure.

tests: F-1/OPT time is not part of the six-year H-1B clock; only H and/or L time counts.
message: I've been in the US five years on F-1 and OPT. Does that mean I only get one year of H-1B?

expected_facts.counts_toward_six_years: time spent in the US under H and/or L classification

must_say: (h)(13)(iii)(A) counts six years spent under section 101(a)(15)(H) and/or (L)
F-1 and OPT time is not H or L time
must_not_say: F-1 time counts against H-1B limit

tests: L-1 time counts toward the six-year limit, tested with an exact date.
message: I was in L-1A status in the US continuously from January 15, 2023 to January 14, 2025, then moved straight to H-1B on January 15, 2025 and have been in the US the whole time. When is my six-year limit?

expected_deadlines.what: six-year limit reached
expected_deadlines.derivation: L and H time are combined; continuous presence from 2023-01-15; six years ends 2029-01-14 (Sunday). H-1B portion = 2025-01-15 to 2029-01-14 = 4 years.

must_ask_for: any days outside the US during L-1 or H-1B time (they can extend the date)
must_say: Time in L status counts together with H time against the six-year maximum

tests: After the maximum is used: one year abroad requirement, brief-trip rule, and the cap interplay with recapture versus a new admission.
message: I will use up my six years on September 30, 2028 and plan to leave. How long do I have to stay outside the US before a new H-1B, and would a new H-1B be cap-subject?

expected_deadlines.what: earliest date one year abroad is complete (if the person leaves on 2028-09-30)
expected_deadlines.derivation: 'immediate prior year' outside the US: 2028-10-01 through 2029-09-30. A new petition could be approved/admission granted after that; exact counting day is not specified.

must_say: Residence and physical presence outside the US for the immediate prior year, except brief business or pleasure trips
Brief trips do not interrupt the year but do not count toward it

If the person was previously counted against the cap for that 6-year period, recapture does not require a new cap number; a new period of admission under section 214(g)(1) is the alternative ((h)(13)(iii)(C)(2))
must_not_say: A one-day visit restarts the clock
Brief trips count toward the year abroad
ambiguity_note: The text says 'the immediate prior year'; it does not state the day count convention, and whether a new petition after a year abroad is cap-subject depends on the statute and exemption status beyond this corpus.

tests: Lengthy-adjudication-delay exemption needs 365 elapsed days; tests the arithmetic and refuses green-card strategy.
message: My six years end February 28, 2027. My employer filed my labor certification on August 20, 2025. Can my H-1B be extended beyond six years, and for how long at a time?

expected_facts.extension_increments: up to 1 year at a time
expected_facts.filing_in_advance: petition may be filed within 6 months of the requested start date

expected_deadlines.what: 365 days elapsed since labor certification filing
expected_deadlines.derivation: 2025-08-20 plus 365 days = 2026-08-20 (Thursday); as of 2026-11-16, 453 days have elapsed.

must_ask_for: whether the labor certification was required and is non-frivolous, and that the person is the named principal beneficiary
must_say: At least 365 days since the labor certification filing makes the person eligible beyond six years
Approvals are in up to 1-year increments until the stated final-decision events
must_not_say: Which green card category to choose
That the application will be approved

tests: Cap-gap end date: April 1 of the fiscal year being requested (April 1, 2028 for FY2028), not April 1 of the filing year and not October 1; ends earlier at the validity start date if approved.
message: My OPT ends August 31, 2027. I was selected and my employer filed a cap-subject H-1B petition requesting change of status with an October 1, 2027 start date. How long does my F-1 status and work authorization last?

expected_deadlines.what: cap-gap extension ends if the petition is approved with start Oct 1, 2027
expected_deadlines.derivation: (f)(5)(vii)(A): until 'April 1 of the fiscal year ... or until the validity start date of the approved petition, whichever is earlier'. Validity start 2027-10-01 is earlier than 2028-04-01.

expected_deadlines.what: outer limit while the petition remains pending or if validity start is later
expected_deadlines.derivation: FY2028 runs 2027-10-01 to 2028-09-30; 'April 1 of the fiscal year' = 2028-04-01 (Saturday).

must_say: Status and OPT work authorization are automatically extended from the OPT end date
Extension ends at the earlier of April 1, 2028 or the approved validity start date
It ends automatically on rejection, denial, revocation or withdrawal of the petition or denial/withdrawal of the change of status request
must_not_say: The extension always lasts until October 1

tests: Cap-gap end tied to the validity start date when that is earlier than April 1.
message: OPT ends May 31, 2027. Cap-subject petition filed June 1, 2027 for change of status, requested start December 1, 2027, selected registration. When does my cap-gap end if it's approved?

expected_deadlines.what: cap-gap end if approved with start date Dec 1, 2027
expected_deadlines.derivation: Earlier of 2028-04-01 and validity start 2027-12-01 is 2027-12-01 (Wednesday). Filing on 2027-06-01 is exactly six months before Dec 1, so it meets (h)(2)(i)(J).

must_say: Cap-gap ends at the validity start date (Dec 1, 2027) because it is earlier than April 1, 2028
The petition must have been timely filed, which includes being within the six-month rule

tests: Catches the stale Oct 1 rule: a pending petition on Oct 1 no longer ends the cap-gap (April 1 now). Conflicts with USCIS Policy Manual text that still says October 1.
message: It's October 1, 2027 and my H-1B petition is still pending. My OPT ended in August. A friend says cap-gap ends today and I have to stop working. True?

expected_deadlines.what: outer limit of the cap-gap extension
expected_deadlines.derivation: (f)(5)(vii)(A): April 1 of FY2028 (fiscal year began 2027-10-01) = 2028-04-01 unless the petition is approved earlier with a validity start date, or the petition/change of status is rejected, denied, revoked or withdrawn.

must_say: Under the current regulation the extension runs to April 1 of the fiscal year, not October 1
It ends sooner on approval (at the validity start date) or on rejection, denial, revocation or withdrawal

tests: Consular notification instead of change of status means no cap-gap extension.
message: My employer ticked consular notification on the petition because I might visit home. I was selected and my OPT ends June 30, 2027. Do I still get the cap-gap?

expected_facts.cap_gap_requires: a timely filed, nonfrivolous cap-subject petition requesting a change of status, with start date in the fiscal year and no status violation
expected_facts.termination: upon rejection, denial, revocation or withdrawal of the petition, or denial or withdrawal of the change of status request, even if the petition is approved for consular processing

must_say: (f)(5)(vii)(A) applies to a petition 'requesting a change of status'
Without a change of status request there is no automatic extension; the person would need to depart and seek admission in H-1B status
must_not_say: Cap-gap applies to consular processing petitions

tests: Cap-gap applies only to petitions subject to section 214(g)(1)(A); cap-exempt petitions do not get it.
message: I'm on OPT ending May 15, 2027. A university filed a cap-exempt H-1B change-of-status petition for me in February with an August 2027 start. Will the cap-gap cover May to August?

expected_facts.cap_gap_applies_to: H-1B petition subject to section 214(g)(1)(A) of the Act

must_say: (f)(5)(vii)(A) covers a petition subject to section 214(g)(1)(A) of the Act; a cap-exempt petition is outside that language
The student should plan around the OPT end date and the 30-day period; ask the DSO or counsel

tests: Student already in the post-OPT departure period when the petition is filed: status extension applies if timely, but whether work authorization resumes is not settled by the text.
message: My OPT ended May 31, 2027. My employer filed the cap-subject change of status petition today, June 29, 2027, for an October 1 start. I have a fixed-period I-94. Am I in cap-gap and can I work?

expected_facts.status: automatically extended per (f)(5)(vii)(A) if the petition is timely filed, nonfrivolous, and the student has not violated status
expected_facts.work_authorization: text says 'any employment authorization granted under 274a.12(c)(3)(i)(B) or (C)' is extended; the EAD had already expired when the petition was filed

expected_deadlines.what: last day of the 30-day period (fixed admission)
expected_deadlines.derivation: (f)(5)(v): additional 30-day period from the end date of the post-completion OPT employment authorization. 2027-05-31 + 30 days = 2027-06-30 (Wednesday). Filing on 2027-06-29 is inside the period.

must_say: The petition was filed within the 30-day period, so it is timely for status purposes
During the 30-day period the student could not work, and the text does not clearly authorize work to resume; USCIS policy says the student is not employment-authorized in that case
Confirm with the DSO or an attorney before working
must_not_say: You can work starting today under cap-gap
ambiguity_note: (f)(5)(vii)(A) extends status and 'any employment authorization granted'; the EAD expired before filing. USCIS Policy Manual (Vol. 2, Part F, Ch. 5) says no employment authorization is extended in that case; the regulation text does not say so expressly. Present both and do not assert work authorization.

tests: Same facts in the departure period but filed after day 30 under fixed admission vs inside the 60-day legacy period: outcome flips on admission type; status expired before filing means no cap-gap and no change of status absent discretionary excuse.
message: My OPT ended May 20, 2027. My employer filed the cap-subject change-of-status petition on June 25, 2027. Am I covered by cap-gap?

expected_deadlines.what: last day of departure period, fixed-period admission
expected_deadlines.derivation: May 20 + 30 days = June 19, 2027 (Saturday). Filing June 25 is 6 days late.

expected_deadlines.what: last day of departure period, legacy D/S admission (properly maintaining status on 2026-09-15)
expected_deadlines.derivation: 8 CFR 214.1(m)(1): 'plus the departure period of 60 days'. May 20 + 60 days = July 19, 2027 (Monday). Filing June 25 is inside it.

must_ask_for: whether the I-94 shows a fixed admit-until date or D/S, and whether the student left and re-entered after September 15, 2026
must_say: For a fixed-period admission the 30-day period ended June 19, so status expired before filing and a change of status generally cannot be approved ((248.1(b)); late filing may be excused only in discretion for extraordinary circumstances)
For a legacy D/S student the 60-day period runs to July 19, so filing June 25 is timely

tests: Contradictory facts: the claimed cap-gap cannot exist because the petition was filed after the departure period ended under either regime.
message: My OPT ended December 31, 2026 and my employer filed my H-1B change of status on April 5, 2027. I'm on cap-gap, right? I've been working since.

expected_deadlines.what: end of 30-day period (fixed admission)
end of 60-day period (legacy D/S)

must_say: Both periods ended before the April 5 filing, so the petition was not timely for cap-gap
Working after OPT ended is unauthorized employment
A change of status cannot be approved for someone whose status expired before filing, except by discretionary excuse ((248.1(b))

tests: Travel while a change of status is pending: departure abandons the application.
message: My cap-subject change of status petition is pending and my OPT already ended. Can I fly home for two weeks and come back?

expected_facts.effect_of_departure: USCIS will consider the change of status application abandoned if the alien departs while it is pending

must_say: Under 8 CFR 248.1(f), departing while a change of status application is pending means the change of status is considered abandoned
A student whose OPT already ended would also face reentry questions as an F-1; speak to the DSO or counsel before travelling
must_not_say: You can freely travel and return in F-1 status
Travel has no effect on the pending change of status

tests: 60-day grace period date arithmetic after a layoff, including a Sunday boundary and counting convention.
message: I'm on an H-1B valid until September 30, 2028. I was laid off and my last day of work was October 30, 2026. Until what date can I stay without a new petition?

expected_deadlines.what: end of the 60-day period
expected_deadlines.derivation: Day 1 = 2026-10-31; Oct 31 = day 1, Nov 30 = day 31, Dec 29 = day 60 -> 2026-12-29 (Tuesday). Shorter of 60 days and the end of the validity period (2028-09-30) is 60 days.

must_say: Up to 60 consecutive days or until the end of the authorized validity period, whichever is shorter
Once during each authorized validity period
May not work during the period unless otherwise authorized
May apply for an extension of stay or change of status during it
must_not_say: You may keep working during the 60 days
ambiguity_note: The text does not say whether the last day of employment or the next day is day 1. Counting from the day after gives 2026-12-29; counting the last day of work as day 1 gives 2026-12-28. A good answer states its convention.

tests: 'Whichever is shorter': the petition validity ends before 60 days run out.
message: I was laid off on November 1, 2026. My H-1B approval notice shows validity until November 25, 2026. Do I get a full 60 days?

expected_deadlines.what: end of grace period
expected_deadlines.derivation: 60 days from Nov 1 reaches 2026-12-31, but (l)(2) says 'up to 60 consecutive days or until the end of the authorized validity period, whichever is shorter'. Validity ends 2026-11-25, which is earlier.

must_say: The period ends at the end of the validity period when that comes first
(l)(1) allows admission up to 10 days after validity ends, but that is about admission, not working or maintaining status
ambiguity_note: 214.1(l)(1) adds up to 10 days after the validity period to the admission period; the text does not say whether those days extend the (l)(2) period. Best answer: November 25 under (l)(2), mention the I-94 may show later.

tests: Whether the H-1B grace is discretionary and currently in force; the system must state it is in the 2026-10-14 text but may be shortened or eliminated by DHS.
message: Is the 60-day H-1B grace period guaranteed? Did it change in 2025 or 2026?

expected_facts.discretion: DHS may eliminate or shorten this 60-day period as a matter of discretion

must_say: 214.1(l)(2) provides up to 60 consecutive days, once per validity period
DHS may eliminate or shorten it as a matter of discretion, so it is not an absolute entitlement
The regulation text current to October 14, 2026 shows no change to this provision (cannot see individual-case determinations)
must_not_say: The grace period is guaranteed in every case

tests: In the grace period a new employer's portability filing: later-of rule, filed before the authorized period ends, no unauthorized employment.
message: I was laid off October 30, 2026 and my 60 days run to December 29. A new company files an H-1B petition for me today, December 15, and asks for a December 21 start. When can I start working for them?

expected_deadlines.what: earliest start under portability
expected_deadlines.derivation: (h)(2)(i)(H): authorized to start 'upon the filing ... or as of the requested start date, whichever is later'. Filing 2026-12-15, requested start 2026-12-21 (Monday); later = 2026-12-21.

must_ask_for: whether the person worked anywhere without authorization since last admission
that the petition is nonfrivolous, requests an extension of stay, and was filed before the authorized stay ended
must_say: Work may begin on the later of the filing date and the requested start date
(h)(2)(i)(H)(1) requires filing before the authorized period of stay expires and no unauthorized employment
must_not_say: You may work during the grace period before filing

tests: Admission-regime trap for the post-OPT period: 30 days for a fixed-period admission, 60 days for legacy D/S; system must ask which applies for a user who traveled.
message: My STEM OPT ends August 31, 2027. I traveled to India in December 2026 and came back in January. How many days after STEM OPT do I get before I must leave or change status?

expected_deadlines.what: end of period if re-admitted for a fixed period (departed and re-entered after 2026-09-15)
expected_deadlines.derivation: 8 CFR 248.1(e): an F alien who departed and applies for admission on or after 2026-09-15 is admitted to the program end date not to exceed 4 years; (f)(5)(v): 30 days after the OPT end date. 2027-08-31 + 30 days = 2027-09-30.

expected_deadlines.what: end of period if still on legacy D/S status (not the case if re-entered)
expected_deadlines.derivation: 8 CFR 214.1(m)(1): 60-day departure period; 2027-08-31 + 60 days = 2027-10-30 (Saturday).

must_ask_for: the admit-until date or 'D/S' on the I-94 issued at the January re-entry
must_say: A student re-admitted after September 15, 2026 is admitted for a fixed period and gets the 30-day period under (f)(5)(v)
Students who stayed in the US in D/S status and were maintaining it on September 15, 2026 get the 60-day period under 214.1(m)(1)

tests: Portability start date is the later of filing and requested start; tests a requested start date after filing.
message: I'm in H-1B status with an approved petition valid until 2028. A new employer filed a new H-1B petition for me today, November 20, 2026, and asked for a December 1 start. Can I start working for them on November 21?

expected_deadlines.what: earliest start at the new employer
expected_deadlines.derivation: (h)(2)(i)(H): 'upon the filing ... or as of the requested start date, whichever is later'. Filing 2026-11-20 (Friday), requested start 2026-12-01 (Tuesday); later = 2026-12-01.

must_ask_for: whether any work outside authorized H-1B employment occurred since last admission
must_say: The later of the filing date and the requested start date
Eligibility: lawfully admitted in H-1B status, nonfrivolous petition filed before the authorized stay expires, no unauthorized employment since last admission

tests: Portability requires H-1B status already provided; a student with an approved petition but not yet in H-1B status cannot port.
message: My H-1B change-of-status petition was approved with a start date of October 1, 2027, and I'm still in F-1 on cap-gap. Another company offered me more money and filed an H-1B petition for me yesterday. Can I start there now under portability?

expected_facts.portability_requires: lawfully admitted into the United States in, or otherwise provided, H-1B nonimmigrant status

must_say: Portability is only for someone who has been admitted or provided H-1B status, which has not yet happened here
Without portability, the person is not authorized to start with the new petitioner until that petition is approved ((h)(2)(i)(D))
must_not_say: You can start at the new company on the filing date

tests: A denied portability petition: work stops on adjudication; the text expressly protects a return to the earlier petition only for successive portability petitions, so the system must not overstate.
message: I'm on H-1B valid until 2029 at Acme. BetaCorp filed a transfer petition and I started working there under portability. USCIS just denied BetaCorp's petition. Do I have to stop working, and can I go back to Acme?

expected_facts.employment_under_portability: ceases automatically upon adjudication of the petition ((h)(2)(i)(H)(2))
expected_facts.return_to_prior_employer: (h)(2)(i)(H)(3)(iii) says denial of a successive portability petition does not affect the ability to continue or resume working under a previously approved petition that remains valid, if H-1B status was maintained or the person was in a period of authorized stay and has not worked without authorization

must_say: Work at BetaCorp under portability stops on the denial

Whether the person can resume at Acme depends on the Acme approval still being valid, status having been maintained and no unauthorized employment; the text states this expressly for successive portability petitions, and the system should say it is not certain the same wording covers a first portability petition
Consult an immigration attorney before returning to work
must_not_say: You must leave the US immediately
You can keep working at BetaCorp
You can definitely return to Acme
ambiguity_note: (H)(3)(iii) is written for a 'successive' portability petition. A first portability petition denial is not expressly addressed; the same result is plausible but not stated. A responsible system flags the gap.

tests: Unauthorized employment since last admission defeats portability.
message: In August I did two weeks of paid freelance work on the side while in H-1B status. A new employer filed a transfer petition for me today. Does portability still let me start?

expected_facts.portability_requires: has not been employed without authorization from the time of last admission through the filing of the petition

must_say: Portability requires no unauthorized employment from last admission through filing
Freelance work outside the H-1B petition is the kind of unauthorized employment that matters; the person should see an attorney, not rely on a tool
must_not_say: It will be fine because it was only two weeks

tests: Cap-gap termination on denial is textual, but the text is silent on any leftover departure period; the system must not invent 30 or 60 days.
message: My H-1B change of status was denied while I was on cap-gap. My OPT ended in May. How long do I have to leave?

expected_facts.text_says: the automatic extension of status and employment authorization terminates automatically upon rejection, denial, revocation or withdrawal of the petition, or denial or withdrawal of the change of status request

must_say: The extension ends automatically on denial
The regulation text does not state any further departure period for this situation; it should not be assumed
Talk to the DSO or an immigration attorney immediately
ambiguity_note: DHS/USCIS web pages say a 60-day grace follows termination; the 2026 fixed-period rule changed the general departure period to 30 days, and (f)(5)(vii)(B) itself gives none. A responsible system flags the gap and does not state a number as law.

tests: Withdrawal causes immediate automatic revocation with no appeal; refile eligibility is not settled by the text.
message: My employer said it withdrew my approved H-1B petition 'to refile it better'. Is my approval still valid, can I appeal, and can they reuse my lottery selection?

expected_facts.effect_of_written_withdrawal: approval is immediately and automatically revoked
expected_facts.appeal: automatic revocations may not be appealed

must_say: A written withdrawal immediately and automatically revokes the approval
Automatic revocations cannot be appealed
Whether a refiled cap-subject petition can rely on the same selected registration is not addressed clearly by the text; the petition must be based on a valid registration ((h)(10)(ii))
must_not_say: The approval is still valid until you are notified
ambiguity_note: The text says a cap-subject petition must be based on a valid registration but does not address reuse after withdrawal. The system should give the automatic revocation facts and say reuse is not answered by the regulation.

tests: Who may appeal a denial and what cannot be appealed, without giving procedural deadlines not in the corpus.
message: My H-1B petition and my change of status were both denied. Can I appeal, and who files it?

expected_facts.petition_denial: may be appealed under 8 CFR part 103 (the petitioner is notified of the right to appeal)
expected_facts.extension_or_change_of_status_denial: no appeal from a decision to deny an extension of stay or change of status to the alien

must_say: A denied petition may be appealed under part 103 (by the petitioner)
There is no appeal from the denial of the extension of stay or change of status
The beneficiary is not an affected party for a petition appeal (8 CFR 103.3(a)(1)(iii)(B)), so the employer files it
Appeal deadlines are in 8 CFR part 103 (103.3(a)(2)(i) says 30 days after service of the decision) and not in the H-1B provisions; any deadline given must not be invented
must_not_say: You can appeal the change of status denial
A deadline that is not in 8 CFR part 103

tests: Revocation-on-notice rebuttal deadline: 30 days from receipt, not from the date on the notice.
message: My employer got a notice of intent to revoke my H-1B on November 3, 2026. When is the response due and who sends it?

expected_deadlines.what: rebuttal deadline
expected_deadlines.derivation: (h)(11)(iii)(B): rebuttal evidence 'within 30 days of receipt of the notice'. 2026-11-03 + 30 days = 2026-12-03 (Thursday).

must_ask_for: the date the notice was actually received (the 30 days run from receipt)
any different time period stated in the notice itself
must_say: The petitioner (employer) submits rebuttal evidence within 30 days of receipt
If revoked on notice, the revocation may be appealed under part 103 ((h)(12)(ii))
must_not_say: Revocation takes effect immediately on notice

tests: Employer reporting that the employee no longer works there triggers automatic revocation and the grace-period and return-transport rules.
message: My boss says he told USCIS I no longer work there, effective today. What happens to my H-1B and my status? Is the company supposed to pay my flight home?

expected_facts.effect: the H-1B approval is immediately and automatically revoked upon the petitioner's notice that the beneficiary is no longer employed
expected_facts.status: cessation of employment alone is not a failure to maintain status for up to 60 consecutive days or the end of validity, whichever is shorter, once per validity period
expected_facts.return_transport: employer is liable for reasonable return transportation costs if the alien is dismissed before the end of the authorized period; voluntary resignation is not dismissal

must_ask_for: whether the person was dismissed or resigned
the petition's validity end date
must_say: Approval is automatically revoked and cannot be appealed
The 60-day (or shorter) period under 214.1(l)(2) applies, work is not allowed during it
Return transportation cost liability depends on dismissal
must_not_say: You can keep working during the 60 days

tests: Borderline job: 'any bachelor's degree' is not enough, but a range of directly related fields can be; the system must not give a verdict.
message: My job title is marketing coordinator. The job posting says any bachelor's degree is fine. Is that a specialty occupation?

expected_facts.general_degree: a position is not a specialty occupation if attainment of a general degree, without further specialization, is sufficient
expected_facts.range_of_fields: a range of qualifying degree fields is allowed if each is directly related to the duties of the position

must_ask_for: the actual degree requirement the employer states
the specific duties
which of the four criteria the employer will rely on
must_say: A requirement of any bachelor's degree without specialization does not make it a specialty occupation
A range of fields can qualify if each is directly related to the duties
At least one of the four criteria in (h)(4)(iii)(A)(1)-(4) must also be satisfied
USCIS decides; no prediction
must_not_say: Marketing is never a specialty occupation
ambiguity_note: Depends on the duties and the degree fields the employer requires; the text defines the test but cannot classify the job. A responsible system states the test and asks for facts.

tests: 'Normally' means usual, not always: an employer that usually requires a degree can meet the criteria.
message: Our company usually requires a bachelor's in computer science for this role but we hired one person without one once. Does that kill the specialty occupation argument?

expected_facts.normally: conforming to a type, standard or regular pattern; characterized by what is usual, typical, common or routine; does not mean always

must_say: Under (h)(4)(iii)(A)(5), 'normally' does not mean always
A single exception does not by itself defeat the criteria; the petition must still meet at least one of (A)(1)-(4)

tests: Beneficiary equivalency arithmetic: three years of specialized work or training for each missing year of college.
message: I only finished two years of a four-year computer science degree but have lots of work experience. How many years of experience equal a bachelor's degree for H-1B purposes?

extra_requirements: theoretical and practical application of specialized knowledge
experience gained working with peers, supervisors or subordinates who have the degree or equivalent
recognition of expertise evidenced by at least one listed type of documentation
other_routes_to_equivalence: credit evaluation by an official with authority at an accredited college
evaluation by a reliable credentials evaluation service

expected_counts.what: years of specialized training and/or experience needed
expected_counts.derivation: Missing college years = 4 - 2 = 2. (D)(5): 'three years of specialized training and/or work experience must be demonstrated for each year of college-level training the alien lacks'. 2 x 3 = 6 years.

must_say: The regulation's rule of thumb is three years of experience per missing year (here six years)
The experience must meet additional conditions and recognition of expertise
USCIS determines equivalence; other evidence routes exist
must_not_say: Two years of experience are enough

tests: Third-party placement: the end client's requirements, not the staffing company's, are most relevant.
message: I work for a staffing company and I'm placed at a bank full-time. Whose degree requirements matter for deciding if my job is a specialty occupation?

expected_facts.rule: if the beneficiary is staffed to a third party (contracted to fill a position in the third party's organization and part of its hierarchy), the actual work must be in a specialty occupation and the third party's requirements are most relevant

must_ask_for: whether the person becomes part of the client's organizational hierarchy or merely provides services to the client
must_say: For a person staffed to a third party the third party's requirements are most relevant
Staffed means filling a position in the third party's hierarchy, not merely providing services to it
must_not_say: Only the staffing company's requirements count

tests: Compares change of status and consular processing from the text without telling the user which to pick.
message: Should I go for change of status or consular processing for my H-1B? I have OPT through 2027.

expected_facts.change_of_status: requires continuing to maintain nonimmigrant status; leaving the US while pending abandons it; gives access to cap-gap if the petition is cap-subject and timely
expected_facts.consular: no cap-gap extension; the beneficiary is admitted in H-1B status from abroad for the petition validity

must_ask_for: whether the person plans to travel before the start date
whether OPT/STEM OPT or the departure period expires before the start date
must_say: Explains each route's effect on cap-gap and on travel
The choice is a personal and legal decision; consult the DSO or an immigration attorney
must_not_say: You should choose change of status

tests: Admission window for consular processing: 10 days before validity, no work until validity starts.
message: My petition was approved for consular processing with validity October 1, 2027 to September 30, 2030. When can I enter the US and when can I start work, and how long can I stay after it ends?

expected_deadlines.what: earliest admission
expected_deadlines.derivation: (l)(1): admitted for the validity period 'plus an additional period of up to 10 days before the validity period begins'. 2027-10-01 minus 10 days = 2027-09-21 (Tuesday).

expected_deadlines.what: earliest day to work in H-1B
expected_deadlines.derivation: (l)(1): 'Unless authorized under 8 CFR 274a.12, the alien may not work except during the validity period.'

expected_deadlines.what: end of post-validity admission period

must_say: Up to 10 days before and after the validity period for admission
No work outside the validity period
must_not_say: You can start working on arrival

tests: Terminology confusion: selection in the lottery is not approval and not H-1B status.
message: i got picked in the h1b lotery!!! thats my approval right?? can i just start working for them when my opt ends

expected_facts.selection: permits the petitioner to file a cap-subject petition within the filing period; it is not an approval

must_ask_for: whether the employer will file a change-of-status petition within the filing period
OPT end date
must_say: Selection only lets the employer file the petition
The petition must still be filed within the notice's filing period and approved
Cap-gap may bridge the time only if a timely filed change of status petition exists
must_not_say: You can work for them on OPT end without a petition

tests: Typos plus missing facts: the system must ask for the pivotal facts, then give the conditional answer.
message: my opt end jun 15 2027 n company file hone b petition apr 1 start oct 1 how long can i work after opt

expected_deadlines.what: cap-gap end if all conditions hold and approved with Oct 1, 2027 start
expected_deadlines.derivation: OPT end 2027-06-15; extension runs to the earlier of 2028-04-01 and the approved validity start 2027-10-01 -> 2027-10-01. Filing April 1 for an Oct 1 start meets the six-month rule.

must_ask_for: whether the registration was selected
whether the petition is cap-subject and requests change of status (not consular notification)
whether the I-94 shows D/S or a fixed date (for the fallback departure period)
must_say: If the petition is a timely, cap-subject, change-of-status petition filed from a selected registration, work authorization is extended after OPT until the earlier of April 1, 2028 or the approved start date
must_not_say: Definitively yes without confirming the facts

tests: Approval is not the start of status: H-1B status starts on the validity date, until then the student relies on F-1/OPT and cap-gap.
message: my h1b got approved in april so im h1b now right? my opt ends in june so i dont need to worry

expected_facts.validity: the petition's validity period shows when H-1B employment may begin

must_ask_for: the approved validity start date on the I-797
whether the petition requested change of status or consular notification
must_say: Approval does not by itself start H-1B status; the validity period on the approval notice controls ((h)(9)(i)(A), (h)(9)(ii))
If OPT ends before the validity start, cap-gap is what bridges, and only for a timely cap-subject change-of-status petition
must_not_say: You are in H-1B status now
You do not need to worry

tests: Decline lottery odds but explain the weights that the text does give.
message: I'm wage level IV with a US master's. What are my exact chances of being selected this year?

expected_facts.can_say: level IV is entered four times; there is also a separate advanced degree exemption selection
expected_facts.cannot_say: any probability, since it depends on the number of registrations, not in the regulation

must_say: The regulation gives weights, not odds
Level IV is entered four times
The system cannot give a selection probability
must_not_say: You will almost certainly be selected

tests: Fees and the $100,000 proclamation are outside the regulation; the system must not state amounts or applicability.
message: How much does the H-1B registration cost, and I heard employers now have to pay $100,000 per H-1B. Does that apply to my change of status?

expected_facts.regulation_content: registration fee is non-refundable and due when the registration is submitted; ACWIA fee applies to initial H-1B, initial extension and change of employer, with exemptions for institutions of higher education and related nonprofits; dollar amounts are in 8 CFR 106.2 (not in the corpus)
expected_facts.proclamation: the $100,000 payment arises from a presidential proclamation (Proclamation 10973 of Sept 19, 2025, extended by Proclamation 11069 of Sept 18, 2026 to Sept 21, 2027), not from 8 CFR 214.2(h)

must_say: Dollar amounts are not in the regulation text this tool covers; check USCIS and 8 CFR 106.2
The $100,000 payment is not in 8 CFR 214.2(h); whether it applies to a change of status is outside this tool
Decline to say it does or does not apply
must_not_say: The registration fee is a specific dollar figure stated as law
The $100,000 payment does not apply to students
The $100,000 payment applies to every student
ambiguity_note: The XML contains no mention of the proclamation. Applicability to change of status petitions is a USCIS/State Department policy question outside the corpus, and could not be verified from the regulation. The system should decline, not guess.
